summary.name: Dylib Hijack Scanner (DHS)
summary.one_liner: A macOS utility that scans your computer for applications that are vulnerable to dylib hijacking or have already been hijacked.
use_cases: Check a Mac for apps that could be abused by dylib hijacking
Detect whether any installed application has been hijacked
Scan the full file system for hijackable applications
Save scan findings as JSON for later review
Triage flagged dynamic libraries against known false positives
summary.what_it_does: DHS scans the computer for applications that are susceptible to dylib hijacking or have been hijacked, and lists them under 'Vulnerable Applications' and 'Hijacked Applications'. The user starts a scan by opening DHS.app and pressing 'Start Scan'. Preferences allow a full file-system scan, detection of weak hijackers that abuse weak imports, and saving findings as JSON to dhsFindings.txt in the app's directory. The author says DHS favors reporting false positives over missing malicious hijackers, so flagged items may be benign. The FAQ suggests checking the known false positives list, submitting the dylib to VirusTotal, or inspecting it with strings.
notable: Distinguishes vulnerable apps from actually hijacked apps
Optional full file-system scan and weak hijacker detection
Open source, with source code linked from the page
caveats: Flagged items may be false positives; the author favors over-reporting
No per-application patches exist for vulnerable apps, according to the FAQ
